review_type: single AI curator; full final answer read; model identity visible
rationale: Accurate narrower conclusion, appropriate energy/viability and uptake alternatives, defined peptide-bond assay with detection controls, time-course and matched-energy comparison, and useful selectivity counterscreens. Source existence and notice status are kept separate from scientific validity and intent.
reference_guardrails: The reported endpoint is puromycin incorporation. Do not require candidates to assert independently established protein synthesis suppression.
Concurrent 50% ATP and 60% incorporation reductions do not establish causal order or a quantitative transfer function. ATP amount is not adenylate energy charge.
A full cell-free translation assay can be inhibited outside the peptide-transfer reaction. Isolate the reaction or separately control charging, factors and regeneration.
A negative assay constrains its tested species, chemical form and conditions. It is not a universal refutation; positive controls alone do not cover every context mismatch.
Biochemical direct action and the cause of a cellular phenotype are distinct. ATP rescue or early timing alone does not exclude mixed mechanisms.
Selectivity requires a defined comparison scope. Cross-species ribosome activity need not contradict selectivity for peptide transfer over unrelated targets.
No DOI supplied is not no DOI exists. No recorded notice is not proof of reliability. Existence, provenance, editorial status and scientific support remain separate.
The reference suggestions about ATP matching and complete cell-free negatives are prospective checks, not uniquely identifying interventions.
